| [NOTE-064](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-064.md) v2 | Bourrat 2023, a coarse-graining account of individuality | Bourrat proposes that a partition of particles into collectives defines individuals when the "projected" prediction (coarse-grain at t1, then evolve the coarse-grained state) differs from the "truthful" one (evolve at the fine grain, then coarse-grain at t2) by δC = C_T − C_P < θ, across many traits (Eqs. 1–2). | [NOTE-100](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-100.md) | Bourrat — Reproducees, reproducers, Darwinian individuals | Being reproduced (a reproducee), being able to reproduce with some autonomy across backgrounds (a reproducer), and being a Darwinian individual (a reproducer with high reproductive causal control) are distinct statuses — so genes in multicellular organisms are, like hearts, mere reproducees that serve larger reproducers, and material overlap is needed for reproduction by reproducers but not by reproducees. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-114](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-114.md) | SEP — Biological individuals | Biological individuality cannot be settled by equating individuals with organisms: the space of biological individuals is better mapped along the evolutionary (Darwinian) vs physiological (living-agent) distinction, with organisms, some parts of organisms and some groups of organisms each filling distinct regions — genes are Darwinian individuals without being agents, honey-bee colonies arguably likewise. | Skimmed |

| [NOTE-148](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-148.md) | Baedke — The Organism (Cambridge Element) | The organism is a "nexus concept" whose organizational (inward) and relational (outward) dimensions have to be integrated. | [NOTE-149](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-149.md) | Chakravartty — Ontological Priority and non-eliminative OSR | Non-eliminative OSR's core thesis, that relations are ontologically prior to their relata because they determine the relata's identity, fails.
